A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 3–5 and Appendix C report original hallucination detection and mitigation experiments, attention analyses, ablations and statistical tests.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an AMBER benchmark evaluation in Appendix C.5 and Table 13.

M1.justification: The VAR/SVAR measures, two-layer MLP detector and intervention averaging absolute attention scores across heads are unchanged. The added layer-division discussion explains existing ranges without revising the procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on AMBER's 1,004-image generative task, whereas v1 uses COCO-derived evaluation data. This is a bounded extension of the existing object-hallucination task, evaluated on LLaVA-1.5-7B.

E2.justification: Greedy decoding, beam search, OPERA, VCD and PAI remain the mitigation comparators; internal confidence remains the detection baseline. AMBER uses the same five mitigation comparators, and the PAI-component comparison is retained.

E3.justification: The added AMBER evaluation uses LLaVA-1.5-7B, a 512-token generation limit and CHAIR, Hal and Cog metrics. Existing COCO sample sizes, the MLP's 80:20 split, model configurations and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The layer-range and balance-factor ablations, attention-head visualizations and qualitative examples are retained. AMBER adds benchmark scores; Appendix C.6 adds interpretation without a new ablation or diagnostic experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same one-tailed t-tests, hypotheses and statistical reporting in Appendix C.2 and Tables 8–11. The AMBER addition introduces no repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New Table 13 reports AMBER results for six methods: the proposed method obtains CHAIR/Hal/Cog scores of 4.3/20.2/1.2, versus PAI's 4.9/24.4/1.6. These are additional benchmark results, not revisions to the COCO scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(6) remain unchanged. No theorem, proof or formal assumption is added; the new layer-division rationale is conceptual interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central findings about middle-layer visual processing, hallucination detection and training-free attention intervention. AMBER supplies supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.6 interprets early layers as low-level image processing and final layers as supporting grammar and coherence, and clarifies that their widths vary across models. v1 primarily explains the two middle-layer stages. Appendix A's limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link on the first page; v1 provides none. Existing MLP optimizer settings, epoch count, hyperparameter grids and intervention parameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds AMBER, further LVLM and interpretability references, and literature concerning medical, recommendation and driving applications. It removes the Qwen-VL and original Visual Instruction Tuning citations. The central research positioning around visual information processing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose edits, shortens the Section 3 heading, adds appendix subsections and acknowledgments, and updates author/contact information. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds AMBER Table 13, moves the MLP schematic from main-text Figure 8 to appendix Figure 10, relocates Table 12, and adjusts spacing and captions. Table 2 clarifies its relative-change annotations. Existing scientific figures are retained.

improvement.justification: AMBER provides additional validation beyond COCO, while the code link and layer-division explanation improve documentation and clarity. These are useful but limited gains: AMBER covers one model, the added layer-role explanations lack new diagnostic tests, and subjective layer selection remains an acknowledged limitation.
